brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut: they keep 5.9% profit vs peers' 3.8%, so there's room in their price.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price cut on rigid plastic packaging.
priceAsk.target: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc for induction-wad caps (market asks ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical); scale similar cuts across all SKUs.
priceAsk.basis: They keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% at similar firms — that extra 2.1 points lives in the price they charge us. The open market shows modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume, so our target sits inside what the market will bear.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (move from 30 days to 15 days) in exchange for half the price cut — about 6% off.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days earlier costs us ₹22.57 L in cash freed up for them. They borrow money at about 12.19%, so 15 days early is worth roughly 0.5% of the invoice to them — but their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d at peers, so faster payment is valuable. Trade it for a 6% price cut (half their borrowing rate, reflecting the cash relief).

brief.financialLeverage: Chemco is healthy — CRISIL A+ rating, keeps 5.9% profit, and grew 22.1%/yr — so little risk they'll fold. But their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d at peers, meaning cash is tighter than it looks. We're only 0.59% of their ₹937.60 Cr revenue, so we're small to them — but their growth appetite and cash bind give us two levers: offer faster payment for a price cut, and dangle volume commitment (they're hungry for new orders). Push firmly on price; the profit gap vs peers (5.9% vs 3.8%) proves there's margin to give. The A+ rating means you can press hard without tipping them over.

evidence.point: They keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% at similar firms — 2.1 points more margin than peers.
Their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d at similar firms — so cash is tighter and they'll value faster payment.
They borrow at about 12.19%, so paying 15 days early is worth roughly 0.5% of the invoice to them.
We're ₹5.49 Cr of their ₹937.60 Cr revenue — just 0.59% — so we're small but can still trade volume commitment for price.
They grew sales 22.1%/yr, so they want new orders — leverage that hunger.
Market ask for 28 mm caps is ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume — our target sits in that band.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms — with revenue ₹2569.83 Cr and health score B (65/100). A strong second-source candidate already in our data.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma); strong, profitable — a robust alternate for bottles/closures.

risks: We're only 0.59% of their revenue, so walking away won't hurt them much — keep the tone firm but fair, and lead with the profit-gap evidence.
Their rating is CRISIL A+ and health is solid (B, 64/100) — they don't need our business to survive, so the squeeze must be justified by the peer profit gap and market pricing, not distress.
Their cash cycle (104d) is longer than peers (79d), but free cash flow is strong at ₹118.43 Cr — so they're not desperate; position faster payment as a convenience worth trading, not a lifeline.
The market-ask verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR' with only 'modest headroom' — so a 10–15% ask is at the edge of what the market supports; be ready to settle at 8–10% if they push back hard.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to close the gap between what you charge us and what similar packaging firms keep as profit — your 5.9% vs their 3.8% — and we're ready to pay faster or commit more volume to get there.
